subject: Rate scan and competitor pricing — follow up on Redwood hosted API
messages:
From: Ethan Caldwell <ethan.caldwell@nimbushealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick: can you match OpenAI/Together rates for our pilot?

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. Procurement asked me to run a competitor rate scan before we move forward with an internal pilot. Attached is a consolidated rate sheet from our RFP (OpenAI, Anthropic, Together, AWS) and our expected monthly token profile.

High level:
- Pilot forecast: ~400M tokens/month peak, ~120M tokens/month steady after month 2.
- We care most about per-token burst cost and the cost for long-context chat sessions.

Can Redwood provide:
1) A baseline hosted API rate card for the above usage (per 1k tokens for generation + embeddings if applicable)
2) Any available competitive discounts or match to the rates in our attachment (we have a 12-month procurement window)
3) Notes on where Redwood typically wins vs. OpenAI/Anthropic (latency, KV cache, batching) so our finance team can justify price differences

If we can get a written rate match or a committed discount, we'll include Redwood in the pilot shortlist and start procurement paperwork.

Attachments: Nimbus_RateCard_Comparison.xlsx (spreadsheet), Nimbus_Expected_Usage.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Ethan Caldwell
VP Engineering, Nimbus Health
ethan.caldwell@nimbushealth.com
+1 415-555-0199

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2026-11-18T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick: can you match OpenAI/Together rates for our pilot?

Ethan —

Really appreciate the detailed attachment; helpful context. Short answer: we can be highly competitive and have a few levers that make our hosted API materially cheaper for your workload. Below is an initial baseline and a proposed commercial path.

Baseline hosted API list rates (estimate for pilot profile):
- Text generation (1k tokens): $0.030 (prompt+completion combined)
- Embeddings (1k tokens): $0.010 (if you use embeddings for search)

Commercial proposal options:
A) Self-serve / pay-as-you-go: match list above; no commitments
B) Pilot reservation (3 months commit): 20% off list + $10k pilot credits to offset upfront testing costs
C) 12-month commitment (annual): 30% off list + tiered volume discounts as you cross 1B tokens/month

Why Redwood can win vs competitors for your use case:
- Latency & long-context: our KV cache and continuous batching reduce per-request latency in multi-turn chat (we can show session-level traces)
- Cost controls: auto-batching and prefix caching typically reduce your effective tokens charged versus naive calls to other hosted providers
- Predictable throughput: dedicated pools for customers on reserved plans avoid noisy neighbor spikes you sometimes see on hyperscalers

Next steps I suggest:
1) Quick 30-minute call with finance/procurement to align on the commercial model you prefer (I can bring Rafael from pricing)
2) If you share a preferred target per-1k-token number, we can rapidly map to a commitment band and send a term sheet

I copied Rafael (pricing lead) to propose an approved discount band and Monica from CS to scope observability needs during the pilot.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0123

--
Attachment: redwood_proposed_term_sheet.pdf (pdf)

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-18T11:28:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick: can you match OpenAI/Together rates for our pilot?

Folks — forwarding Nimbus's request. Quick notes from pricing desk:

- Their attached XLS shows effective blended competitor rates around $0.021–$0.025 per 1k tokens for generation at pilot volumes (including promotions).
- Standard allowable pre-approved pilot discount: up to 20% for a 3-month commitment. Anything beyond 20% needs commercial approval (we can approve up to 25% for Strategic deals with manager sign-off).

Questions for Soojin:
1) Do they require an invoiceable committed spend (yes/no) or is a simple billing credit acceptable for pilot?
2) Are they sensitive to an SLA or required to be in a private deployment? (affects pricing)

I recommend offering: 25% off list for a 3-month pilot if they sign a short MSA addendum and we apply a $15k pilot credit. If they push for parity with the lowest competitor line-item, we should ask for a 6–12 month commit.

Rafael
Director, Pricing Operations
